question.explanation:
To differentiate a logarithm with base $a,$ we use the formula

\[ \dfrac{\textrm{d}}{ \textrm{d} x}\left( \log_a x \right)= \dfrac{1}{x\ln a}. \]

Therefore,

\begin{eqnarray} \eqalign{ f'(x) & = \dfrac {\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}x} \left( \log_5 {x} + 5\ln x\right) \\[5pt] & = \dfrac {1}{x \ln 5} + 5\left(\dfrac {1}{x}\right) \\[5pt] & = \dfrac {1}{x \ln 5} + \dfrac {5}{x}. } \end{eqnarray}

question.text: Given the function $y=2\ln x+3e^x,$ the slope of the tangent line at $x=1$ is
question.explanation:
To find the slope of the tangent at a given point, we have to find $\dfrac {\textrm{d}y}{\textrm{d}x}$ at that point.

Taking the derivative, we have \[ \eqalign{ \dfrac{\textrm{d}y}{\textrm{d}x} &=\dfrac{\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}x}\left(2\ln x+3e^x\right)\\[5pt] &=2\dfrac{\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}x}\left(\ln x\right)+3\dfrac{\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}x}\left(e^x\right)\\[5pt] &=2\cdot\dfrac{1}{x}+3e^x\\[5pt] &=\dfrac{2}{x}+3e^x \,. } \]

Therefore, the slope of the tangent at $x=1$ is \[ \eqalign{ \left.\dfrac {\textrm{d}y}{\textrm{d}x}\right|_{x=1} &=\left.\left(\dfrac{2}{x}+3e^x\right)\right|_{x=1}\\[5pt] &=\dfrac{2}{1}+3e^1\\[5pt] &= \bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{2+3e} \,. } \]

question.text: Given the function  $y=\ln x + 2\cdot 3^x - 1$, find the instantaneous rate of change at $x=1.$ Do not round the answer.
question.explanation:
To find the instantaneous rate of change at a given point, we have to find $\dfrac {\textrm{d}y} {\textrm{d}x}$ at that point.

Taking the derivative, we have \begin{align} \dfrac{\textrm{d}y}{\textrm{d}x}&=\dfrac{\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}x}\left(\ln x + 2\cdot 3^x - 1\right)\\[5pt] &=\dfrac{1}{x}+2\cdot 3^x\ln (3). \end{align}

Therefore, the instantaneous rate of change at $x=1$ is \[ \eqalign{ \left.\dfrac {\textrm{d}y} {\textrm{d}x}\right|_{x=1} &=\left.\left(\dfrac{1}{x}+2\cdot 3^x\ln (3)\right)\right|_{x=1}\\[5pt] &=\dfrac{1}{1}+2\cdot 3^1\ln (3)\\[5pt] &= \bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{1+6\ln (3)} \,. } \]
